Hi [~accountid:712020:548c71a6-d1f4-404d-9c5e-482bc0de371a] - I understand that. What I am saying is what is the rationale for only having a privacy notice that covers our first engagement (and not a privacy notice that would _also_ cover where we decide to enter an agreement with the content creator)?

Privacy notices are not agreements - they are purely transparency documents. The same privacy notice could apply to both content creators that we do contract with, and those that we do not. As such, my preference would be to have a privacy notice that covers both scenarios.

If the first point at which we are processing the content creator’s data is when they enter their details into the form, I would also be minded to provide the privacy notice via a hyperlink in the form, rather than with the T&Cs (although this is not a deal-breaker). I will take another look and provide revised comments.

Hi!  Thank you for tagging.

According to the BF T&Cs with Partners - Invoicing and Payments:

{quote}T​he Partner undertakes to issue valid cash register’s receipts for the Goods Price. The issued cash register’s receipts are transported to the Client together with the Goods. Bolt shall prepare and issue to the Client informational receipt for the Goods Price on behalf of the Partner. {quote}

It is clear that the providers are obligated to provide cash register’s receipts (aka invoices) to the eaters.  Just like when you eats in the restaurant, you will get a bill (showing what you ordered, VAT if any) and a receipt after you paid.  As promised, Bolt provide the informational receipt to the eaters via email / Bolt App, but it is not an official documents and will not replace any responsibility of the providers in terms of invoicing.  We should align on this point and majority of the countries work like that unless there are regulations saying Bolt should bear any invoicing obligations for the providers.  In LV, Bolt is not required to issue food invoices on behalf of partners by tax law.  

It may be meaningful to communicate with the partners on this point too to make sure they provide the order receipt to eaters.

Hi [~accountid:5fc514a09592df00761a5d3d] ,

Here is a brief assessment of the situation:

*a) What is the claim?*
The user claims the reduced top speed of the scooter at <25% battery constitutes:

* Defective performance: The scooter failed to meet expected performance.
* Lack of transparency: The speed limitation was not disclosed, violating §312d BGB.
* Breach of contract: The scooter did not meet the expected functionality.

The user requests a pro-rata refund for affected rides and process adjustments to block or flag scooters with <25% battery as “limited functionality.”

*b) What is required under §312d BGB?*
Providers must disclose material limitations that affect usability before the contract is concluded.

* If the speed reduction at low battery was not reasonably foreseeable or disclosed, it could be seen as a breach of information obligations.
* The claim might be considered to be true if this non-information and the ‘defect’ significantly impacted usability. Though this depends on whether the issue is deemed material.

*c) Impact of T&Cs and Scooter design:*

* The T&Cs do not guarantee a minimum speed, weakening the user’s claim of defective performance. Expectations about speed are subjective unless explicitly promised elsewhere (e.g., marketing). Did we make such promises?
* The speed reduction is a deliberate feature to prolong battery life, not a defect. Users are also responsible for checking battery levels pre-ride (Annex A, Section 1.1), further supporting our position. Correct?

*d) Result:*

I conducted a quality pre-analysis for the ATI _"User in Vehicle Related Accident"_ and reviewed approximately 150 tickets. During this review, I identified several common mistakes and issues among agents handling these cases. Below is a summary of the main findings:

# *Agents Rarely Call the Users:*
#* The guidelines do not explicitly state that agents should call users to investigate and resolve cases. There is [a link|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/38007?country=global&language=en#handling-low-and-moderate-safety-reports] within the [KB article|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/50191?country=global&language=en] that leads to this information, but not all agents tend to follow it or explore each link.
#* New agents or those who may not be aware of updates are less likely to perform the necessary calls. This information is only available in the KB article _"🚨🛴_ [_Micromobility Safety Case Handling Workflow_|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/38007?country=global&language=en#handling-low-and-moderate-safety-reports]_"_. It would be beneficial to move this information to the first point of the article or reinforce it as a reminder for all rental safety agents. Here is the ticket examples, where the phone calls are not made -[ ticket 1|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/487289382]; [ticket 2|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/491851515]; [ticket 3|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/487760626]. 
#* Additionally, agents often fail to add internal notes after phone calls. Many cases are handled in languages other than English, which makes quality checks more challenging when the call language is different.
# *Unclear Guidelines for Handling Inbound Calls:*
#* In Germany, a significant number of cases involve inbound calls. However, there are no clear guidelines on how to handle such cases. The closest KB article is _"🚨🛴_ [_Micromobility Third-Party Safety Workflow_|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/49800?country=global&language=en#details-are-not-provided]_,"_ but it does not fully address this scenario.
#* Some agents manage to find the relevant details but still ask users to contact support via the app instead of resolving the issue during the call, for example - [ticket 1|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/488387499]; [ticket 2|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/490198622]; [ticket 3|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/499620656]. 
#* Clear instructions or reminders on how to handle inbound calls, especially in Germany, should be added to the workflow.
# *Not Logging the Safety Cases on time:*
#* The KB article _"_[_User In Vehicle Related Accident [Micromobility]_|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/50191?country=global&language=en]_"_ begins with the instruction to "Fill out the [*Global Event Assessment Tool*|https://www.cognitoforms.com/Taxify1/globaleventassessmenttool2] and follow the [*Micromobility Safety Case Handling Workflow*|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/38007?country=global&language=en]." This can be confusing for agents, causing delays in logging safety cases even when all the information is available.
#* Often, agents wait to log the tool only after investigating or receiving a response from the user, which sometimes takes several days, here are examples, the agents are not logging the case even though they have already enough information - [ticket 1|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/489170925]; [ticket 2|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/490025975]; [ticket 3|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/498600736]. 
# *Incorrect or Missing Global Assessment Tool Comments:*
#* Comments are often added incorrectly or not added at all. Common issues include:
#** Adding comments in one bulk instead of across relevant sections.
#** Failing to add comments in all required places, such as tickets, user profiles, and order pages - [ticket 1|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/485879354]; [ticket 2|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/479730068]; [ticket 3|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/494455123]. 
#* While instructions for adding comments are available [in the KB|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/47241?country=global&language=en#leaving-internal-notes], they are not included in the main article _"_[_User In Vehicle Related Accident [Micromobility]_|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/50191?country=global&language=en]_"_. Adding a disclaimer at the end of the article, reminding agents to add comments in all required areas, would improve quality in backend actions, user profile actions, and beehive comment actions.
# *Poor Empathy and Problem Acknowledgment:*
#* Agents struggle to show empathy effectively. For example, responses like "I am sorry to hear that you had an accident; I hope you are OK" sound robotic and insincere - [ticket 1|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/485879354]; [ticket 2|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/492884184]; [ticket 3|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/499970132].
#* Agents need to understand that empathy is not just about acknowledgment but should be reflected throughout the entire communication, this could be a great reminder to the agents to understand how to improve empathy and how to properly show it in safety-related cases.
# *Not following the Building Blocks logic:*
#* Agents frequently forget to apply building blocks correctly in safety cases, therefore the seamless interaction is scored down.
#* Common issues include sending acknowledgment separately, using unnecessary blocks or sentences, and failing to close the case properly - [ticket 1|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/497551321]; [ticket 2|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/494455123]; [ticket 3|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/487760626]. 
# *Inconsistent Use of Problem Markers:*
#* Agents do not always follow guidelines when adding problem markers, even though the global assessment tool and KB article instructions cover this process.
#* For instance, if a report is made 2–3 days after an incident and the scooter has been in use during that time, a problem marker may not be necessary. Including this clarification in [the KB article|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/50191?country=global&language=en] could help reduce errors.

h3. Additional Observations and Suggestions for the[ KB Article|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/50191?country=global&language=en]:

# *Problem Marker Usage and Informing OPS:*
#* In the KB article, it states:
_"❗ If there were any damages or injuries as a result of the incident, add a 'Problem Marker' to the Rental vehicle and forward the issue to your local Rentals Operations."_
#** In practice, when a vehicle is blocked, it automatically becomes inactive. Agents typically add a description to the problem marker, including a link to the ticket, but they do not inform Operations (OPS) about it.
#** This process discrepancy should be clarified in the KB article to reflect the actual steps taken by agents and whether informing OPS is necessary.
# *Handling Unsafe Parking Cases:*
#* The KB article states:
_"In case of Unsafe Parking Causing Injury Or Structural Damage, if the rental was left in an unsatisfactory position or place."_
#** There is ambiguity about what constitutes "unsatisfactory parking." For example:
#*** In Germany, parking between the sidewalk and the side of the road where cars are parked is acceptable. If the scooter overturns for some reason, it may not be the customer's fault.
#*** The customer's fault should be determined only in cases where they intentionally push the scooter, leave it overturned, place it in the middle of the sidewalk, or leave it in an entirely inappropriate location.
#** Adding clear examples of acceptable and unacceptable parking scenarios would help agents make better judgments.
# *Determining the Root Cause:*
#* The [KB article|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/50191?country=global&language=en] does not specify how to determine the root cause of an incident. For instance:
#** Should the root cause be based on the customer’s explanation, the third party’s statement, the police report, or visual evidence such as pictures or videos?
#** Providing guidance on prioritizing evidence and handling conflicting accounts would reduce ambiguity for agents.
# *Access to Geolocation Data:*
#* The[ KB article|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/50191?country=global&language=en] states:
_"Use Geolocation to determine the rental/order by following the Micromobility Safety Case Handling Workflow, and update the Assessment Tool with any information we might find."_
#** In practice, OS agents (the ones handling safety cases) do not have access to geolocation data. This creates a gap in their ability to follow the instructions provided.

Hello, here is bank payments of the client.

+*(*) MID-ORDER SUBSTITUTION*+

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Overview*
{panel}

* Substitution = A driver who has been given a journey to complete by Bolt passing that journey onto another driver to complete.
** i.e., Driver A after indicating he will provide a ride can allocate (in-app) to Driver B. Rider updated with new driver details and revised ETA.
** This is similar to fleet model, but not the same. Only applies to private drivers.
*** In fleet markets, we enable arguments that Bolt doesn’t restrict the ability for fleet drivers to make subbing arrangements between themselves. We do not necessarily offer a functionality for subbing.
** See RFC [here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1u8YgjTLlRmyqEFGgOksqgKwyvXR6a1RV4ZnH_PKZpAc/edit?tab=t.0].
** This is being introduced as Bolt Link was not found to be sufficient.
* Process would be as follows:
** Driver A has a section in the Driver Portal where substitution is explained.
*** In this section, Driver A can input details of Driver B. 
** Driver B would receive an email (and/or in-app notification) containing an invitation to be a substitute for Driver A. Driver B would have to accept this invitation.
** Driver B would then provide documents to confirm they are eligible.
*** Driver B must have passed ID verification / docs checks, to be in the running. Bolt is entitled to check these documents for safety purposes:
**** (i) that the Driver is who they say they are (e.g. ID check); and 
(ii) the Driver can lawfully fulfil rides (market specific but for example: transport licence, insurance documents, car documents, car licence, etc).
*** Driver A will *not* be reviewing Driver B’s documents. However, Driver A will be notified about receipt of the docs.
** Driver A accepts order.
*** Substitution is only possible while pick up phase, not before, not after.
** Driver A can nominate Driver B to take the order (where Driver B is online).
*** This would be near the ‘Cancel order’ button. Clicking this would show their nominations that are still online and don’t have orders.
*** On the Bolt side, we would then cancel the existing order try and create a new order try for the selected driver.
** Driver B then needs to confirm the order. 
*** If they do not, then:
**** (i) Order goes back to Driver A (or anyone else nominated by Driver A).
**** (ii) If Driver A rejects, then the order is passed to regular rematching logic.
** Rider would see this rematching as it happens in the app.
*** Rider would be shown Driver B’s name and license plate. App would state “This order is served by Driver B on behalf of Driver A”.
* Invoicing and payments will be issued to the account of driver who actually fulfilled the order.
* Driver A can remove Driver B any time from their list.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Privacy Analysis*
{panel}

* This seems like a good initiative and something that is not overly intrusive. As such, I do not imagine there is anything that will act as an obvious blocker here.
** Would be worth conducting a {color:#4c9aff}*PPRA*{color} on this, seeing as the intention is for it to have global application.
** Nevertheless, this overlaps with {color:#ff5630}*ICO Investigation*{color} (work allocation). Not a high-risk item, but we need to be careful what we say and ensure that documents are in place.
* *Categories of data*:
** PPRA: [Link|https://www.cognitoforms.com/bolttechnologyo%C3%BC/preliminaryprivacyriskassessment/entries/1-all-entries/107]
** Categories of data themselves are not always new (primarily a new purpose).
** Regarding invitations:
*** Name and email address of Driver B.
** Sign-up flow:
*** ID check / verification docs of Driver B. No criminal offence data (only licence docs), but {color:#36b37e}*check*{color}.
*** It appears that existing verification docs (current drivers)
** During orders:
*** Driver A’s list of substitutes [new].
*** The fact that Driver be is a substitute of Driver A, as well as their status (i.e., approved or not) [new]
*** Journey flow (i.e., acceptance and substitution).
*** Status of substitution (i.e., “This order is served by Driver B on behalf of Driver A”) [new].
** This all seems proportionate.
* *Data subjects:*
** Existing drivers
** New drivers (who have not yet signed up)
* *Purposes*:
** Various processing purposes are at play here.
** Invitations:
*** To invite them to the Bolt platform. This is new, and should be included in a separate privacy notice. As an interim measure, I would recommend {color:#4c9aff}*disclaimer language in the invitation*{color}.
*** If Driver B does not accept, we should {color:#4c9aff}*delete their data within a reasonable period (e.g., 30 days)*{color}.
** Checking ID / verification docs:
*** Falls under ‘To authenticate your account and verify your identity’. We would want to update this to include verification as a substitute.
** Substitution during orders:
*** Falls under the ‘connecting drivers with passengers’ banner, but we will need a new subset under this category ‘Allowing drivers to substitute an order’ - {color:#4c9aff}*this should be reflected in the updated privacy notice*{color}.
* *Legal bases*:
** Sending invitations:
*** We cannot practically rely on consent here. Nor can we rely on contractual necessity (as the new driver has not asked for this).
*** As such legitimate interest would be the most likely legal basis (interest in facilitating substitution and increasing customer base).
**** We should {color:#4c9aff}*conduct a LIA*{color}.
** Sign-up flow:
*** We can primarily rely on contractual necessity here.
**** Otherwise, any synchronisation of docs (e.g., using docs Driver B has already uploaded to the platform to confirm their eligibility) would rely on legitimate interest, and so need {color:#4c9aff}*a LIA*{color}. Long-term, this could be incorporated into a general LIA re synchronising docs on the platform.
*** However, if we are doing any biometric checks (e.g., where Driver B provides their ID to confirm eligibility for substitution), we may need to get consent / fresh consent. {color:#36b37e}*Check*{color}.
** Mid-order substitution:
*** This would most likely be based on legitimate interest (as substitution is not necessary for any contract between Driver A and Bolt, nor Driver B and Bolt). Interest in improving driver flexibility and ensures service continuity.
**** As such, we should {color:#4c9aff}*conduct another LIA*{color}, unless the facts suggest otherwise.
*** However, this may depend on contractual relationship (e.g., sub-processors) - but this is unlikely in the circumstances.
* *ADM*:
** No obvious ADM here. No DPIA should be needed (although note that a DPIA is recommended by the PPRA - TBC).
* *Transparency*:
** As noted above, for new drivers, we should include transparency language so it is clear what personal data processing is going on here. This also limits the risk profile re invisible processing.
** As noted above, we need to update the purpose of processing in the privacy notice (and possible legal basis). Otherwise, should already be covered in the draft.
** Once a driver goes from being a third party to a user, {color:#4c9aff}*we should provide them with the privacy notice*{color}. Same goes for current Bolt drivers going for substitution option.
* *Back-end / DSRRs:*
** Will we be retaining records of original orders before they were substituted? {color:#36b37e}*Check*{color}.
** Subject to redactions, we may want to consider {color:#4c9aff}*whether DSAR responses should be updated*{color} to include substitution details.
** We need to check what is the {color:#36b37e}*process for Driver B wanting to be removed from Driver A’s list*{color}.
** We should make sure {color:#4c9aff}*only Driver B’s name is visible*{color} in Driver A’s app, and not their contact details.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Conclusion*
{panel}

* No obvious blockers from a Privacy POV.
* In terms of Privacy action items:
** Prepare PPRA and potentially LIAs.
** Update the privacy notice.
** Consider updating DSAR process.
* Business action items:
** Ensure that disclaimer language is included in the invitation to Driver B.
** Ensure only Driver B’s name is visible in Driver A’s app, and not contact details.
** Include privacy notice links at the relevant times.
** If Driver B wants to be removed from Driver A’s list, ensure that there a process for them to do so.
** If Driver B does not accept invitation, we should delete their data after a reasonable period (e.g., 30 days).
* Questions:
** Contractual relationship between Driver A and Driver B?
** Retention of substitution records (i.e., original order and substitution)?
*** (We should be doing this for audit purposes and also to investigate and prevent fraud).
** Check what docs we are asking for from Driver B. Any biometric processing? Are criminal records checks?
** If a driver is suspended / banned from the platform, presumably they would not be able to use substitution as a means of getting around this?

+*DRIVER SHOPPING*+

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Overview*
{panel}

* GFT are still obtaining external counsel advice on this. However, PP prepared a memo on this [here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1XyPhqs5tiXTFL_LvHMab0TYW0nRlg1pNlcT1_wzjiQc/edit?tab=t.0].

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Privacy Analysis*
{panel}

* We need to be careful this does not undermine anything in the {color:#ff5630}*ICO Investigation*{color}.
** I need to {color:#4c9aff}*review LIAs / DPIAs already conducted*{color} in this area, and consider.
* No massive change to the types of personal data / purposes. Does not appear to be intrusive / high risk from a purely data processing perspective.
* Legal basis would most likely be contractual necessity here (as connecting passengers with drivers).
** However, worth considering if a {color:#4c9aff}*Legitimate Interest Assessment*{color} is needed here for good measure.
* Does not obviously raise ADM issues. Passenger makes the selection.
* Need to ensure that purpose / legal basis / feature is covered in the {color:#4c9aff}*Privacy Notice*{color}.

+*(*) PRICE BIDDING*+

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Overview*
{panel}

* Purpose of the feature is to allow riders and drivers to agree on price (see [here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1YIpsN41I3qPANFb9AIY3ytbwdUvV1BcGer9M1R_vnDc/edit?tab=t.0]).
** Currently, drivers will be able to select a minimum price per mile that excludes them from the dispatch queue.
** NB. Driver counter-offer falls within the same remit.
* Process looks like this:
** Suggested price initially presented to rider is based on standard order price + dynamic price. 
*** Bolt still sets the baseline price. This baseline is based on dynamic pricing / surge / etc.
** During order creation and right after it, rider can adjust their proposed price.
*** This goes to -10% or +30% as a range.
** Order goes out to nearby eligible drivers.
*** I need to {color:#36b37e}*check if there is any change to how eligible drives are found*{color} (apparently it is “_per our ride finish probability analysis_”). However, it sounds like Blast Dispatching will be deployed here.
** Upon order acceptance, driver can counter-offer.
** Rider then needs to confirm the final price.
* It looks like this has been / is being launched in a lot of RoW markets.
** {color:#36b37e}*Ask Alon if he has previously reviewed this feature*{color}.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Privacy Analysis*
{panel}

* This is relevant to the {color:#ff5630}*ICO Investigation*{color} (price setting). 
** However, this is likely to be positive, rather than negative. Ultimately, this gives users more control over price. We just need to make sure this is done legitimately and not undermined in our submissions.
** We need to {color:#4c9aff}*update LIA/DPIA previously done for price setting*{color} ([here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C07H44XUFD2/p1730905182952379]).
*** NB. PPRA recommends a DPIA, but this is TBC.
* *Categories of personal data*:
** PPRA: [Link|https://www.cognitoforms.com/bolttechnologyo%C3%BC/preliminaryprivacyriskassessment/entries/1-all-entries/108]
** We are not collecting new data here, just refining the price calculation process. The only ‘new data’ is in the form of bids. I should check with the stakeholders {color:#36b37e}*whether we will be retaining this data / whether it would be visible in order history*{color}.
** The ‘bids’ / negotiation is data being collected directly from the data subjects, and so it is not ‘invisible’. The only ‘invisible’ element is the calculation of the base price, which is not new.
** Data is being processed on a large scale and will involve some dataset combination, but IMO not enough to merit a DPIA. Nevertheless, worth updating the DPIA that currently exists to reflect this.
** Re data minimisation, we should ensure that price bids {color:#ff5630}*do not create profiling of users*{color} (e.g., behavioural data on how often a passenger negotiates prices unless explicitly needed for fraud prevention)
* *Purposes:*
** “_To calculate prices and process payments_” - This is not a new purpose. It is just a refinement of a purpose already in use.
*** We may want to {color:#4c9aff}*update the privacy notice section on this*{color}, just to make it clear.
** The data being collected here appears proportionate / not intrusive.
* *Legal basis:*
** This concerns setting prices, so you could argue contractual necessity here. However, the price is between the driver and the passenger (as much as it is partly determined by Bolt).
** IMO, it would be worth {color:#4c9aff}*conducting a LIA*{color} just to be on the safe side, as Bolt has a legitimate interest in implementing this feature (flexible pricing helps connect drivers and passengers, and benefits both of them(.
* *ADM:*
** The only ‘new element’ of this is the offers / counter-offers (i.e., setting the baseline price and blast dispatching to drivers are separate and already happening). This is done by the users, and so would not count as ADM.
** However, if price bids are fed into the price setting algorithm and influence base estimates over time, then we would need to {color:#ff5630}*consider this more carefully*{color}.
*** e.g., If a passenger frequently offers lower prices, the algorithm might automatically show them higher minimum fares in the future. Alternatively, if a driver rejects too many lower bids, the algorithm might deprioritise them in receiving trip offers. We need to make sure this does not happen.
*** We could still argue that users have control over the final bid (but this would be within a certain range, as determined by the baseline fare, so be careful).
* *Transparency:*
** As mentioned above, need to slightly tweak the relevant row of the privacy notice.
** We will be publishing guidance materials on how price bidding works, which will go some way to keeping this feature transparent.
* *Backend / DSRRs:*
** As mentioned above, we need to check how much of this data we are keeping, as we may need to consider whether we can provide it in response to DSARs.
*** If we do have a good reason to retain it, we should ensure that: (i) users can request a copy; and (ii) we can delete it (if after an assessment we detrmine that we should).
** A recommendable retention period may be for 30 ays after the trip is finished, unless required for disputes or fraud prevention.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Conclusion*
{panel}

* No obvious blockers from a Privacy POV.
* In terms of Privacy action items:
** Check whether a PPRA has already been done on this (Alon).
** Consider whether an LIA is required (or the current price setting LIA needs to be updated).
** Update the privacy notice, and ensure links are provided at the relevant times.
* Business action items:
** Ensure guidance materials are published on how price bidding works.
** Ensure that this data does not result in any profiling of users., nor affect the baseline pricing algorithm / work allocation.
* Questions:
** Any changes to how eligible drivers are found? I assume not.
** Would previous bids remain visible to users in their app?
** Will this influence price estimates / pricing algorithms over time?
** Will we be retaining details about bids / counter-offers? If so, why? Will this be used for other purposes (e.g., analysing pricing trends)?

+*DRIVER TERMS SETTING*+

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Overview*
{panel}

* Under Principal model:
** (1) Bolt UK enters into a transportation services agreement with the driver (“*Bolt UK’s Driver T&Cs*”).
*** Bolt provides transportation services to the passenger and the driver fulfils these services on behalf of Bolt UK.
** (2) Also, BoltUK enters into a journey agreement for a resale of transportation services with the passenger (“*Bolt UK’s Passenger T&Cs*”).
*** Bolt UK enters into the journey agreement as principal. Bolt is providing transportation services that are fulfilled on behalf of Bolt by the driver.
*** The journey agreement between Bolt UK and passengers is formed when the Journey request has been confirmed.
*** By entering into the Journey Agreement, Bolt UK commits to provide the journey and the passenger commits to pay for the journey.
* Under Agency model:
** (1) NewCo enters into a booking agreement with the passenger (“*NewCo’s Passenger T&Cs*”).
*** The driver is the provider of the transportation services. The passenger is informed that the driver has given authorisation to NewCo to negotiate certain provisions of the Journey Agreement (e.g. final price).
*** The contract between the driver and passenger is formed at the pick-up point.
*** Cancellation fee paid directly to NewCo (not to NewCo acting on behalf of the driver) for wasting NewCo’s time trying to find a driver.
** (2) NewCo enters into a booking agreement with the driver (‘*NewCo’s Driver T&Cs*”).
*** NewCo is authorised by the driver to do the following:
**** Negotiate specific provisions on the driver’s behalf;
**** Act as a payment collection agent in exchange for commission; and
**** Act as a compliance agent (to allow NewCo to deal with passenger complaints on the driver’s behalf) in exchange for a service fee.
*** No Commission on the cleaning fee, cancellation fee or similar fees charged to the passenger.
*** Cancellation fee paid by NewCo to a driver as a contractual compensation for NewCo wasting the driver’s time in the event the passenger cancels the journey. No cancellation fee payable by driver to NewCo.
*** T&Cs to prescribe that NewCo is obliged to verify passengers’ cards properly, and if the payments fail, NewCo may pay drivers ‘contractual compensation’ in the amount of fare (excluding commission).
** (3) A journey agreement between the passenger and driver is formed at the pick up point (the “*Journey Agreement*”).
*** The driver must be able to load their personal terms onto the app for passengers to see before the Journey Agreement is concluded.
*** Virtually no written terms here re driver’s obligations to passenger (except for matters of safety).

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Privacy Analysis*
{panel}

* No major changes in processing / purposes. This is more about contractual relationships. Bolt already runs agency / principal models - provided this is not vastly different, there is not much uplift required here from a Privacy POV.

+*DEALING WITH COMPLAINTS / BLOCKS*+

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Overview*
{panel}

* Under Principal model, Bolt handles all customer complaints. Under Agency model, drivers to authorise Newco to handle passengers complaints on their behalf in exchange for a service fee, and NewCo only suspended driver’s access to their account for very serious breaches (i.e., public safety / H&S / quality control of driver services / child safety policies to be  reduced back to the absolute minimum required by law and under different PHO licence conditions).
** Effectively, under Agency model, Bolt should not penalise drivers except for the most serious matters. Passenger complaints should be handled by the driver, and Bolt is not liable for journey quality.
* Links:
** [All UK blocking scenarios|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1d3Y7twClLXOTrlF2rj5lA00mLXaj7evY/edit?gid=323827111#gid=323827111]
** [UK Safety Blocking Scenarios|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1JJiEsLTbsuH46D0OQO-TP2LdO6rEwTc6rsiQhz5MMzk/edit?gid=783263660#gid=783263660] (i.e., Green analysis)
* Proposal that where a driver is suspended under one model, they should be suspended under both Principal and Agency profiles.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Privacy Analysis*
{panel}

* We need to be careful this does not undermine anything in the {color:#ff5630}*ICO Investigation*{color}.
** I need to {color:#4c9aff}*review LIAs / DPIAs already conducted*{color} in this area, and consider.
* No massive change to the types of personal data / purposes. Also, we are being less intrusive here from a data processing perspective.
* Main legal basis here is legitimate interest. This is something we have been doing for a while.
* Main concern here concerns ADM - When suspending drivers, we should {color:#ff5630}*always ensure the decision is subject to human review*{color} unless it is something totally innocuous (e.g., 12-hour block because driver is fatigued).
** If matter is in the driver’s court (e.g., expired ID), we can automate. For Safety cases, there should always be human review.
* Need to ensure that purpose / legal basis / feature is covered in the {color:#4c9aff}*Privacy Notice*{color}.
* Need to confirm {color:#4c9aff}*what data will be processed in the backend*{color}, so that we can deal with DSRRs accordingly.

+*DRIVER / PASSENGER INCENTIVES*+

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Overview*
{panel}

* Drivers:
** Loyalty incentives can be provided on an ad hoc basis, provided that this does not promote _exclusivity_ to drivers.
** To mitigate against VAT risk, incentives should ideally take the form of a _discount to Bolt’s commission_. When communicating with drivers, incentives should be clearly described as reduced (or dynamic) commission rather than using descriptions such as “_driver bonuses_”.
** Safeguards will be established to detect if drivers begin to derive majority of its income from NewCo as a result of loyalty incentive.
* Passengers:
** NewCo to part pay the journey fee on behalf of the passenger (driver fees remain the same).
** Passenger Incentives cannot be referred to as ‘discounts’. Instead, these should be referred to as Bolt making part payment for the journey, or picking up part of the price on behalf of passengers, or similar wording.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Privacy Analysis*
{panel}

* It sounds like we are not massively changing what we are doing here, but more how we are framing it. No obvious Privacy concerns.
* Legal basis would be a mixture of contractual necessity and legitimate interest. Consider if a {color:#4c9aff}*Legitimate Interest Assessment*{color} has already been completed.
* Re safeguards, need to check whether this entails any {color:#ff5630}*ADM concerns / automatic monitoring* {color}of data. Not currently clear, and could possibly require a {color:#4c9aff}*Data Protection Impact Assessment*{color}.
* Need to ensure that purpose / legal basis / feature is properly framed in the {color:#4c9aff}*Privacy Notice*{color}.

+*(*) ABILITY FOR DRIVERS TO CHOOSE THEIR OWN OPERATING MODEL AT ANY TIME*+

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Overview*
{panel}

* This has been [flagged|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C07R84XBR45/p1738767672266479?thread_ts=1738677568.166919&cid=C07R84XBR45] as the highest priority item to review.
* Effectively, drivers will be able to have more than one ‘role’ in the app (aim is to eventually have this as a global model).
** In the context of Project Green / UK, drivers will be able to either fulfil rides for themselves (agency) or for Bolt (principal).
* *Drivers*: In the [app|https://drive.google.com/file/d/1htHY9MmPFt7XRrRprh888ptcgHQ9rZOo/view], presented with a ‘Change Profile’ button in the profile settings. They will be able to select this when not on an active order.
** When pressing this, they will be asked to acknowledge the privacy notice.
*** A clear record / log will be kept of when the driver select this.
** On the home screen, it will be clear to the driver which model they are operating under.
** Each driver profile will have a separate driver_id and data set. 
*** Some of the data can be synchronized across profiles in case of updates (TBD). Profiles will be linked via uniformed partner_id.
** If the driver updates document A or property X in his principal profile, it will be automatically updated in the agency profile (if available), if Driver wants this (option).
*** The exact set of documents that will be updated is TBD.
** Profile suspensions will continue to be handled manually.
* *Riders*: 
** Open opening the app, rider will accept both sets of T&Cs. Rider will then choose a category:
*** Category 1: Principal PHV Bolt by Bolt
*** Category 2: Agency PHV Bolt by Driver
*** Category 3: Agency Black Cab Black Cab by Driver
** Rider is then able to find a driver on this basis and book a trip.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Privacy Analysis*
{panel}

* *Categories of data being processed:* 
** PPRA: [LINK|https://www.cognitoforms.com/bolttechnologyo%C3%BC/preliminaryprivacyriskassessment/entries/1-all-entries/106]
** Primarily, we will not be collecting much by way of new data here, nor processing for new purposes. All that is new is: (1) we are now processing the category of model; and (2) we are allowing drivers to open additional IDs and keeping the data segregated.
** We will now be recording what operating model the driver is under. We will also be collecting data on the type of ride a rider selects. 
*** This is fine, provided it is {color:#4c9aff}*reflected in the privacy notice*{color}.
*** We are collecting this data directly from the users, which at least means it is not overtly ‘invisible’ processing.
** It looks like we will be collecting new documents. {color:#36b37e}*Need to check with Ops what this list of documents is*{color}, and whether it is different from what we are already collecting.
** Arguably, we need to transfer most data between profiles to ensure seamless integration. I doubt this would be disproportionate.
*** However, we should still keep data minimisation principles in mind.
* *Data subjects:* 
** Drivers
** Riders
* *Purposes*: Primary purpose is to create, update and maintain the driver’s Bolt account. 
** However, we will be using a driver’s operating model category in various contexts, each with their own processing context (e.g., to enable a specific type of transportation services, when processing payments etc).
* *Legal Basis:*
** Collecting and storing whether a driver is principal vs. agency:
*** Legal basis here would be contractual necessity. Identification of principal vs agency is necessary to determine which set of T&Cs the driver is subject to at that time (same logic applies for passengers).
** Allowing drivers to switch between models  (and transferring their data between models):
*** Seems that legitimate interest is the most obvious legal basis here (ensuring seamless account integration and ensuring that drivers can switch easily between one model and another).
*** As such, we need to {color:#4c9aff}*prepare a LIA*{color}.
** If we are transferring any sensitive data (e.g., fraud data), then we may need to consider an alternative legal basis. Also, a DPIA should be considered.
* *ADM*: N/A
* *DPIA*: Not required. The only thing that might raise the risk profile here is the fact that we are matching / combining datasets ({color:#36b37e}*check with Ops what this would entail*{color}), but this would be in the user’s reasonable expectations.
** NB. PPRA determined that a DPIA is required. This is probably not strictly necessary, however may be worth completing one for good measure.
* *Transparency*:
** As mentioned above, we need to ensure new data categories are reflected in the privacy notice. We also need to ensure that the {color:#4c9aff}*correct legal entity*{color} is included.
** We also need to make sure that the {color:#4c9aff}*link to the privacy notice is easily accessible*{color} to the user, particularly when they sign both T&Cs.
* *Agreements*:
** Since Bolt UK is managing principal model, and Bolt UK is managing agency model, we should establish a {color:#4c9aff}*JC agreement* {color}for these transfers.
* *Back-end:*
** {color:#4c9aff}*We need clear records of*{color}:
*** The precise dates and times of when drivers are operating under each model, and records of when they switch.
*** Whether a driver is under the agency or principal model (particularly to CS if we are, for example, handling complaints).
** We will need to {color:#4c9aff}*introduce functionalities*{color} to be able to provide this information to drivers in response to DSARs.
*** e.g., We need to be able to source this data in a separated form efficiently, if needs be.
** We should retain the data in line with retention periods for other profile data.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Conclusion*
{panel}

* No obvious blockers from a Privacy POV.
* In terms of Privacy action items:
** We would need to update privacy notice and ensure this is clear.
** We may want to consider an LIA here.
** Implement a JC agreement between Bolt UK and NewCo.
* In terms of business action items:
** Need to ensure clear data segregation and data extraction functionalities.
* Questions:
** Data at-issue: What new documents are we collecting? To what extent are we matching / combining datasets here? Are we transferring any sensitive data?
** What level of optionality will there be re transferring data?

+*(*) DRIVERS CAN SELECT REQUIREMENTS THAT ARE SHOWN TO RIDERS IN THE APP*+

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Overview*
{panel}

* Bolt will include pre-populated requirements (i.e., conditions) that drivers can choose from, which will be displayed to passengers (e.g., no food/drink, no pets, no vaping etc.).
** Drivers pre-select the requirements in their profile settings.
** Does not currently appear to affect work allocation. For example, we do not currently have a functionality whereby passengers can select their favourite features, and drivers with those requirements would be prioritised.
* Process for drivers:
** Driver opens profile and clicks ’Manage conditions / preferences'.
** Driver a pre-populated list of available options (TBD exact options).
*** Aim is not to have free-form text, so as to prevent discrimination.
*** We need {color:#36b37e}*more visibility on what these options are*{color}. Also, we need to know h{color:#36b37e}*ow this will be stored in Admin*{color}, and whether we will be logging changes.
** Driver can manually select / deselect each of them.
* Presentation to riders:
** After order acceptance, rider can navigate to driver details and look through the driver’s T&Cs.
*** Rider would need to proactively search for this info. However, this is under discussion as it may lead to riders having problems with unclear terms from drivers.
*** Riders get free cancellation for custom terms.
** _Alternatively_: Upon acceptance of the order, Rider receives a message in a chat from Driver in a form: “These are additional requirements to have a ride”. If the Rider disagrees they can cancel the trip free of charge in the first N minutes.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Privacy Analysis*
{panel}

* This is not directly relevant to the ICO Investigation.
* *Categories of personal data:*
** This will result in new categories of data being processed about Bolt drivers (i.e., their conditions may amount to personal preferences).
*** None of this will be SCD / sensitive data, provided the options are pre-populated. Similarly, if pre-populated, lowers the risk of discrimination. So low risk.
*** Personal data is coming directly from the data subjects themselves, so not intrusive / invisible.
*** Seems very unlikely that this would require a DPIA.
** No obvious data being processed about riders here.
* *Purposes*:
** To enable / customise the transportations services by connecting passengers and drivers.
*** Not a new purpose, but a refined one. We would need to {color:#4c9aff}*update the row of the privacy notice to cover this*{color}.
* *Legal basis*:
** Contractual necessity would only apply where the contract is between Bolt and the relevant data subject. Here, the relevant agreement would be between the driver and the rider. As such, contractual necessity would not apply.
** Instead, legitimate interest is the most appropriate legal basis (allowing drivers to set trip conditions improves their work environment and reduces disputes, benefiting both drivers and passengers).
*** We should therefore {color:#4c9aff}*prepare a LIA*{color}.
* *ADM*: N/A
** However, need to check whether this will impact ride allocation in any way (e.g., if ‘no pets’ selected, will this affect passengers with assistance dogs?).
*** {color:#ff5630}*Possible risk of equality discrimination*{color} (e.g., passengers with assistance dogs prevented form taking rides). Although minor, worth flagging to business. It is ultimately the driver’s choice here, not Bolt’s.
* *Transparency*:
** As noted above, need to update privacy notice.
** We should ensure that passengers are sufficiently informed of trip requirements before a trip begins.
*** I would prefer the alternative proposal, in which riders do not have to actively search for the additional terms. 
* *Agreements*:
** If we are determining the remit of conditions, arguably there may be a JC situation here. We may want to consider {color:#4c9aff}*including JC terms in the T&Cs*{color}.
* *Backend / DSRRs:*
** As noted above, we need to know how this will be stored in Admin.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Conclusion*
{panel}

* No obvious blockers from a Privacy POV.
* In terms of Privacy action items:
** We would need to update privacy notice and ensure this is clear.
** We should prepare a LIA.
** Consider a JC agreement.
* In terms of business action items:
** Ensure that none of the requirements relate to SCD (e.g., disabilities, health conditions etc.), and do not allow free-form text. 
*** Consider the position with service dogs.
** I would prefer the alternative approach, in which riders do not have to actively search for the additional terms. 
* Questions:
** What are the conditions?
** How will we be storing them?
** Will this impact ride allocation in any way (e.g., if ‘no pets’ selected, will this affect passengers with assistance dogs)?

+*RIDERS CAN ‘FAVOURITE’ DRIVERS*+

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Overview*
{panel}

* After a trip, a rider can ‘favourite’ a driver (see [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3572039989/2021+Q4+Driver+Favoriting]) where they have provided 5*.
** The aim of this feature is so that drivers can build their own contact base.
* A UI element is shown to the rider every time a trip is taken with the previously favoured driver. Would also show the rider ‘Number of rides together’.
** We need to know {color:#36b37e}*what information about the drivers will be retained by the riders*{color}. 
** Also, {color:#36b37e}*will a driver know they have been favourited*{color}? {color:#36b37e}*Can this link be broken by either party pulling out*{color}?
*** [+This article+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3572039989/2021+Q4+Driver+Favoriting] suggests “_Inform driver that they is added to the favorite list_” is out of scope.
** There is an idea to use this feature as an additional component to prioritise drivers. However, Alex Sivkov [mentioned|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ObQsahFHFEqJQubC0bQRNoQc6ZIbjlsQXj39fHvPCjc/edit?tab=t.0] “_In the current form of the proposal - it is only visualization, no adjustment for the matching algorithms_”. As such, fine for now.
*** We should check {color:#36b37e}*what other features this will be integrated with*{color}.
* A UI element will allow the rider to remove the driver from the ‘favourites’ list.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Privacy Analysis*
{panel}

* Provided this does not impact work allocation algorithm, this should not affect the ICO Investigation.
* *Categories of personal data*:
** Drivers:
*** This would result in a new category - whether a driver is favourited or not.
*** Also, number of rides with the rider would be the driver’s personal data.
*** [Remaining data TBC]
** Riders:
*** _Technically_, even though ‘favourited’ status is primarily a driver’s personal data, a rider’s list of their favourited drivers would be the rider’s personal data too. Equally, if a driver is notified that they have been favourited, they may be shown details of the rider that favourited them [TBC].
** This data is not sensitive. Nor is it disproportionate or intrusive if it is purely used for visualisation. No DPIA would be needed.
* *Purpose*:
** This would fall under ‘customising the transportation services’, but needs to be refined as technically this is a new subset.
* *Legal basis*:
** This would be legitimate interest (providing a better user experience by allowing passengers to recognise previously liked drivers is a legitimate business interest).
*** When a rider favourites a driver, it seems unlikely that the functionality would be that the driver would need to consent to allow this to happen. However, driver should be given the opportunity to opt-out.
** We should {color:#4c9aff}*consider a LIA*{color}.
* *ADM*: Provided this is just visualisation, then no obvious ADM here.
* *Transparency*:
** Would need to {color:#4c9aff}*update the privacy notice*{color}.
*** Specifically, update customisation of transportation services role. Also, add new data category.
** We need to make sure that drivers and riders are aware of their favouriting situation.
** We also want to {color:#ff5630}*make sure that not too much driver information is shared with riders*{color} here.
*** i.e., If an account is compromised, we don’t want loads of third-party data being visible.
* *Backend / DSRRs*:
** We need to know {color:#36b37e}*how this data is being stored in the backend (on Admin)*{color}, for the sake of actioning DSARs.
*** Make sure that this is something that we can extract.
** We need to know how drivers can opt out of being a favourite. Ensure that drivers are able to do so easily.
*** If a rider asks for the list of favourites to be deleted, presumably they will have an in-app functionality that allows them to do so. We can refer them there.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Conclusion*
{panel}

* No obvious blockers from a Privacy POV.
* In terms of Privacy action items:
** We would need to update privacy notice and ensure this is clear.
** We may want to consider an LIA here.
* In terms of business action items:
** Minimise the amount of third-party data visible on the app / profiles.
* Questions:
** What information about a favourited driver will be visible on the rider’s app at any given time?
** Will a driver know they have been favourited? Will they be able to object to this in any way?
** How will this be stored on Admin?
** Will this be integrated with any other features (e.g., use for analytics)?

Drops to 0% events that occur above 25% SOC all share a similar behavior. If the battery SOC drops to 0%, then the battery voltage returns to its normal level after approximately 30 seconds. This could indicate that the challenge failed and the battery output was turned off due to anti-theft settings being activated.

Currently, IoT logs do not provide any indication when a challenge fails. However, it is possible to implement a check for this in the IoT system.

The BMS (Battery Management System) includes a field, *“A10D D3 D3 - Anti-theft lock enabled output limit,”* which can be used to determine if the anti-theft output limit has been activated.

* If I order something with a usually short(er) shelf life, I am expecting a shorter amount of time until the expiration date (as the item already has a short(er) shelf life), and I am not entitled to compenation

Dear Hana,

We write in relation to your data subject rights request, which we received on 27 December 2024. Please find our response below.

*(1) Copy of your personal data*

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties. Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

We therefore attach copies of your personal data to which you are entitled.

*(2) Information regarding the irregular activity detected on your account*

As noted in previous messages with you, your voucher was excluded from the calculation as our system detected irregular activity on your account. We are unable to share any further information on such irregular activity, as to share confidential information in this regard could allow third parties to circumvent Bolt’s irregular activity detection and prevention processes, which in turn would undermine the equitable management of the Bolt platform and threaten the rights and freedoms of other Bolt users. We apologise for any inconvenience caused.

*(3) Your rights*

You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. 

If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

*Bolt*

Let’s consider benefits and drawbacks of this decision:

||*Benefits of dont_throw: true*||*Drawbacks of dont_throw: true*||
|Services depended on IMDS can scale out in case of need even if IMDS throws errors|Invalid state of IMDS can affect business logic and lead to bugs and incidents.|

As for me, the only reason to make *dont_throw* *true* by default is to prevent cases when we need quickly scale out service. In other cases this creates risks without benefits.

HPA starts to create new instances with  CPU load > 70%. This means usually we still have time before it affects service performance. And even then k8s has some room before it starts throttling.

Also, engineers can handle errors for IMDS and return default value for them. So, it’s in the service owners power to implement IMDS in a such way to not depend on the remote data source.

From my perspective, we shouldn’t change the current behaviour.

Retrying is basic thing, but might not be the best approach to rely only on retry.

GH responds with additional headers containing information about rate limits, used, available and next reset time. Its possible to utilize that information while making next GH API call. 

|{{x-ratelimit-limit}}|The maximum number of requests that you can make per hour|
|{{x-ratelimit-remaining}}|The number of requests remaining in the current rate limit window|
|{{x-ratelimit-used}}|The number of requests you have made in the current rate limit window|
|{{x-ratelimit-reset}}|The time at which the current rate limit window resets, in UTC epoch seconds|
|{{x-ratelimit-resource}}|The rate limit resource that the request counted against. For more information about the different resources, see [+REST API endpoints for rate limits+|https://docs.github.com/en/rest/rate-limit/rate-limit#get-rate-limit-status-for-the-authenticated-user].|

Also there are Secondary API Limits, e.g. calling same endpoint too often.

[https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api?apiVersion=2022-11-28#staying-under-the-rate-limit|https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api?apiVersion=2022-11-28#staying-under-the-rate-limit|smart-link] 

So, probably its better to introduce our own GH API calls limiter/delayer so the calls stay within the limits.

The ticket is _not_ about making {{dont_throw}} the default for IMDS in general, only for the IMDS, which are used as an implementation detail of {{RemoteConfig}}.

The remote config’s {{getXyzConfig}} methods are already designed in a way that urges the caller with the potential of data inability: one can provide a fallback value, and if they don’t do so, the return value is {{TheConfig | undefined}}.

About benefits - it’s not only a matter of autoscaling. Imagine that the {{config-store}} service is unavailable, and you decide to release your service that has remote config. The new version won’t start due to the {{RemoteConfig}}’s IMDS throwing. So you decide to roll back. But then, the old version does not start either, for the very same reason, and you’re left out with a missing instance of your service, until {{config-store}} is fixed, even though, you _do_ have defaults defined in your service.

+*BACKGROUND*+ (see [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/5550768343/Feature+Overview+Driver+Lead+Automations])

* Targeted deadline by engineering and Product here is end of Feb.
* Currently, there are two types of document review. The first is already automated - the ask here is *_whether the second can be automated as well_*.
** (a) Driver lead automation (when a driver signs up); and
** (b) *Doc renewal* (when an existing driver submits renewed docs through the driver portal).
* Process would look like the following:
** (i) Driver submits updated docs (or registers).
** (ii) Automation reviews the docs.
** (iii) If docs are not acceptance / do not pass, they go to manual review ("_Automation does not decline any documents but leaves them for manual human review_”). If docs are acceptable / they pass, then we go onto the next step.
*** e.g., If text extraction fails, then we fall back on human reviewers.
** (iv) If document requires an online check, this triggers a Beehive task for an external verification by an operations agent (after automation). 
*** These checks include DVLA Online Check, PHL Online Check, PHV Online Check, MOT Online Check.
*** If the online check (manual) is not approved, then driver is blocked and escalated as possible fraud.
** (v) If online check passes (or one is not needed), we then check if there are any custom suspensions on the driver’s profile. If not, they can go online. If there are, then task is assigned to a human reviewer who checks docs that have been auto-accepted, active blocks etc.
*** Driver is then either allowed online or remains suspended based on this review.
** (v) If allowed online, the compliance team reviews the driver profile to ensure that all documents are legible and no fields were missed during automation.
* Plan is to eventually automate all doc renewals in the UK. However, this will be done gradually (one doc at a time). The most likely candidates for the initial launches are:
** UK Driving License
** MOT Test Certificate
** Vehicle Logbook
*** These will then be followed by Insurance documents and the Bank statements across the country, as well as city-specific documents like Private Hire Drivers Licence, Private Hire Vehicle License and PCO Badges.
* Not currently, but _eventually_ automated processes will involve biometric processing (i.e., scanning photo).
* This process will be internal, except for text extraction jobs (where we use Veritas, Bolt’s internal verification service).

+*PRIVACY ANALYSIS*+ (see also [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-44796|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-44796] for work previously done by Gab)

* *Categories of Personal Data*:
** +Profile data+: Name, contact information, address, date of birth (possibly).
** +Identification / verification data+: Driver’s license, transport license, private hire license.
** +Vehicle data+: Vehicle registration details and insurance information, MOT information.
** +Driver compliance data+: Insurance documents, bank statements.
** +Biometric data+: Possibly, if facial recognition used for ID verification.
** +Criminal data+: Possibly, if criminal records checks involved.
* *Data Subjects*:
** Prospective drivers
** Current drivers
* *Sources*:
** Drivers
** External sources
* *Purposes:* To automate the driver lead acceptance and doc renewal processes, including:
** Verification of driver identity and documents.
** Creation of driver accounts.
** Data entry, processing and updating for driver profiles.
*** NB. These purposes are not ‘new’ per se - the proposed change here is the use of automation to pursue the same purposes (e.g., already mostly covered in revised PN under ‘_To authenticate your account and verify your identity_’).
* *Necessity / Proportionality*:
** *Necessity:* Automation is necessary to streamline the driver onboarding process, reduce manual effort, and improve efficiency.
** *Proportionality:* The data collected and processed are proportionate to the purpose of the initiative. Data minimisation principles are applied by collecting only the necessary information for driver verification and account creation.
* *Legal Bases*:
** Privacy notice lists contractual necessity, compliance with a legal obligation, legitimate interest and consent (re biometric processing). These are all valid, depending on the category of data.
*** We need to make sure proper consent is being obtained when this kicks in.
* *Risks / Mitigations*:
** +Transparency+:
*** Risk:
**** The current driver privacy notice is not live. {color:#ff5630}*We do not currently provide enough info on data / purposes / legal bases*{color}. However, current draft does contain third parties / retention etc.
**** In particular, privacy notice should flag that automated processes are used, but that manual review is always in the case of rejections.
**** Drivers will also want a clear explanation of why a particular document was rejected. However, this is mitigated by the fact that we are incorporating human review.
*** Mitigations:
**** Temporary transparency language probably would not be appropriate here, as we are processing a lot of data categories and possibly relying on different purposes. {color:#4c9aff}*Updating the privacy notice*{color} and uploading it should therefore be the priority.
**** Ensure that any {color:#4c9aff}*final outcomes (re rejection) are clearly explained*{color} to the driver.
** +ADM+:
*** Arguably, this is not triggered. Automated processing is involved here, but only to *_approve_* drivers, rather than reject them (only the latter of which, IMO, would produce a legal / similarly significant effect). For rejections, this is always subject to human review.
*** We _could_ consider a DPIA here, although IMO not strictly necessary (as not likely to result in a high risk). We could {color:#4c9aff}*consider conducting a DPIA for good measure*{color} if we are processing biometric / criminal data on a large scale
** +Bias / inaccuracy+:
*** As above, this is mitigated by the manual review element.
* *Next Steps:*
** Ask the stakeholders:
*** Is Veritas provided by a third party (such that we are sharing a lot of personal data with this third party)? If so, presumably we have a data processing / sharing agreement in place?
*** To be clear - Any criminal records / medical records involved?
** Flag to stakeholders:
*** Once Privacy has provided final review (TBC) we can proceed with this.
*** Flag to us when we are considering incorporating biometric checks. We need to make sure proper consent is obtained when this kicks in.
*** We should be clear on explaining to drivers why they were rejected.
** Take the following steps:
*** Conduct a full PPRA.
*** Ensure privacy notice is updated.
*** Consider preparing a DPIA.

Multiple factors cause alerting degradation:

# Some rules (e.g. [IRC] non-OK response ratio, [IRC] Durations) are failing with timeout after 40sec. of evaluation
# Rule evaluation is not isolated. Long-running rule evaluations might affect other rules as the distributor CRON waits for the long-running rules to finish (or to timeout) before starting next evaluation round (see alerting-distributor service MainCron cron)

To fix the current state and prevent degradation in the future, we must:

# Improve the visibility over long-running/not-working rules
# Restore work of the failing rules
# Isolate rule evaluation (e.g. degradation of a single rule should not affect other rule evaluations)

As discussed with sre-telemetry in the [slack thread|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02UNAPUCL9/p1737973627570849], we will do the following:

According to the SRE test, [IRC] Durations rule is executed ~5 times faster (12 sec vs 60sec) in Mimir

Thanks [~accountid:6363e99c76b91b62562fd8f4] / [~accountid:712020:a9ca1df5-fe05-4efc-9bb7-f89fd653ec94] 

I include below an overview of my thoughts, together with some detail on the reasoning. This includes some questions for your attention (these are highlighted in {color:#ff5630}*red*{color}), just to make sure I understand this correctly.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*IN SUMMARY:*

* From a strictly +Privacy POV+, *I do not have any major objections* to the proposed approach, *_provided that_*: (1) it involves asking drivers to manually provide us with what we are already extracting from their documents anyway; and (2) there is a clear and justifiable reason why we specifically need the driver’s DOB / gender / nationality (please confirm).
* The main privacy risk with the proposal is that there is a *transparency gap*, given that we are still in the process of updating our privacy notice (and the current one does not explicitly cover the proposed activity). This is a known risk, and is one that we are working on remedying by updating the privacy notice globally.
* Nevertheless, we generally try to keep our processes uniform across different countries unless there is a pressing need to implement something that is unique to a particular country (e.g., Poland). As such, if the plan is to only do this in Poland, and the rationale behind this is purely to improve Ops processes (rather than due to a legal / pressing need), then from a +process management POV+ *I would advise against country-specific solutions*.
{panel}

*1. Clarification re how this will work in practice / why we need the data*

{color:#ff5630}Do I understand correctly that in Poland we are {color}{color:#ff5630}*_already_*{color}{color:#ff5630} extracting drivers' DOB / gender / nationality from their documents for various purposes, but the current proposal is to instead ask drivers to {color}{color:#ff5630}*_manually provide this information upfront_*{color}{color:#ff5630} (i.e., by filling out a form as part of sign-up)? {color}If so, then this is likely to be consider less intrusive from a Privacy perspective (which is a good thing), as it will be much clearer to drivers that we are collecting this data (and would allow us to side-step issues regarding automated extraction of this data). 
However, if we are to be more upfront about the fact that we are collecting this data, then we can expect questions from drivers about *_why_* we need it. I understand from [~accountid:712020:a9ca1df5-fe05-4efc-9bb7-f89fd653ec94] ‘s last comment that Polish law requires Bolt to keep verification records of drivers - but just to check, {color:#ff5630}are DOB / gender / nationality {color}{color:#ff5630}*_strictly necessary_*{color}{color:#ff5630} here?{color} Or are they just 'nice to haves’? If the latter, then this might raise some Privacy concerns.
Also [~accountid:712020:a7a7d4bc-10ca-44a0-a22e-fa8752330abd] - just to check, if these datapoints are not legally required for Bolt to collect, do we know whether an LIA has ever been conducted on this topic?

*2. Transparency gap*

We need to make sure that we are clearly explaining to users why we are collecting this data, which ordinarily is done through providing them with a copy of our privacy notice.
The current driver privacy notice for Poland does not explicitly cover collecting this data for this purpose, and so technically there is a *transparency gap* here. However, this is a known risk, and we are currently in the process of updating our driver privacy notice globally. The new version should cover this.

*3. Local vs. global processes*

{color:#ff5630}Where is the driver for this initiative coming from? (e.g., Local Ops? Management? Legal? Is it in the MVRA?) Also, is there a pressing need for this initiative, or is it more a nice-to-have?{color}
The reason I ask is creating divergences in our processes between different countries can lead to confusion / complications in how we process data, respond to data subject requests, coordinate and explain our processes etc. As such, *unless there is a pressing need to develop unique processes on a local level, we generally advise against this* - This is not a Privacy compliance point, but more just for the sake of process management.

Happy to discuss if you have any questions! 🙂

+*INTERNAL NOTE*+

* Tier 2 agent created a second ticket [here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/512034101] to send the remaining data. However, I am still not convinced that all of the data has yet been sent (e.g., invoices and tax reports still appear to be missing).
* They have been chased several times, and I will continue to chase. In the meantime, we will proceed with only providing _additional_ info with the Bulk DSAR response (i.e., data not in the data export). 
** (If I try and identify which specific datapoints have not yet been provided and propose sending those with the Bulk DSAR response, this will undoubtedly result in additional confusion / overlap / mess. Although not ideal, the best approach would be to ensure that the data is sent out ASAP via the present thread, and then stick to additional data / info in the Bulk DSAR response).

Hi [~accountid:610279859798100070592384] and [~accountid:6012ab10dc29b4006a594649] we have now received the advice from External Counsel, see summary of advice below: 

# {color:#4c9aff}*DOES TUPE APPLY* {color}

* While the Invitation to Tender (ITT) says that TUPE “may apply” Schedule 7 of the Tender Agreement says that it does apply. 
* TUPE applies if service providers change, transferring employees to the new provider.
* TUPE can apply if there’s a transfer of an "economic entity" or a "Service Provision Change" (SPC). The focus here is on SPC.

{color:#4c9aff}*First Test*{color}{color:#4c9aff}:{color}

* Requires an "organised grouping of employees" whose primary purpose is providing the services.
* Voi UK lists 19 employees 100% dedicated to the services, which suggests this test may be satisfied. However, external counsel would require additional information to confirm if the group is deliberately organised for these services.

{color:#4c9aff}*Second Test*{color}{color:#4c9aff}:{color}

* Assesses if the new contractor's activities post-transfer will remain "fundamentally the same" as Voi UK’s current activities.
* Details on any changes in scope, volume, methods, or location are required to evaluate this.

{color:#4c9aff}*NOTE:* {color}You will note at 2.1.11 external counsel has provided a list of further questions that would need to be clarified in order to assess if +BOTH+ tests are satisfied and if TUPE applies.



# {color:#4c9aff}*IF TUPE DOES APPLY WHAT WILL THAT MEAN IN PRACTICE, WILL BOLT BE REQUIRED TO RETAIN ALL THE EMPLOYEES? IS THERE A CERTAIN TIME PERIOD THEY MUST BE RETAINED BEFORE REDUNDANCIES ARE CONSIDERED?*{color}

*Employee Transfer Rights*: Under TUPE, employees assigned to the services have a legal right to transfer to Bolt on their existing terms and conditions of employment, preserving continuity of service. Employees can choose to object to the transfer, resulting in termination of their employment on the transfer date without redundancy pay or notice compensation.

*Pension Contributions*: For employees in a Defined Contribution pension scheme, Bolt can match the current employer contribution or employee contributions up to 6%. Voi UK's employer contributions are 4.5%, but confirmation is needed that transferring employees have only been in a DC scheme with Voi UK.

*Liability Transfer*: Bolt would inherit significant liabilities, including:

* Accrued employment liabilities and costs.
* Claims for dismissals related to the transfer.
* Collective agreements and trade union recognition.
* Personal injury claims.

*Retention Period and Protections*: TUPE protection does not have a time limit. Employees with over two years of continuous service (18 out of the 19 employees) have statutory protection against unfair dismissal. Dismissals linked solely to the transfer are automatically unfair unless there is an "economic, technical, or organisational" reason involving workforce changes.

*Redundancy and Dismissals*:

* Dismissals for ETO reasons can be fair but must follow normal unfair dismissal rules, including redundancy justification and procedural fairness.
* Bolt must assess whether proposed redundancies are necessary, justified, and reasonably implemented.
* The timing of dismissals may influence whether they are deemed transfer-related but is not decisive.

*Risks*:

* If a dismissal is found unfair, compensation could include up to 52 weeks’ gross pay or the statutory cap of £115,115, whichever is lower. For the listed employees, awards are limited to their annual salaries, which are significantly below the cap.
* In rare cases, tribunals may order reinstatement or re-engagement; failure to comply could result in additional compensation awards.

*Employee Information and Measures*: Bolt must provide Voi UK with details of any measures it plans to take concerning transferring employees. This information is critical for Voi UK to notify affected employees accurately about the transfer.



# {color:#4c9aff}*WE WOULD LIKE TO UNDERSTAND HOW TUPE WILL IMPACT BOLT BEFORE THE TENDER CLARIFICATION PERIOD ENDS CLARIFICATION DEADLINE*{color}

External counsel has highlighted certain points for which additional information would be helpful to assess whether TUPE applies:

*Additional Employees*:Are there other individuals, besides the 19 employees listed, who are engaged in delivering the current services? If so, what proportion of their working time is dedicated to these services? This helps determine whether they are part of the organised grouping focused on the transferring activities.

*Service Grouping*: Are all individuals involved in the services part of a group deliberately organised for the purpose of delivering these services? This ensures compliance with TUPE's focus on an identifiable "organised grouping."

*Service Activity Details*: Are there significant differences between Voi UK's current activities and the services the new contractor will be required to deliver under the proposed Agreement? Any discrepancies might influence whether TUPE applies.

*Pension and Liability Considerations:* Confirmation is needed on whether any of the 19 listed employees transferred to Voi UK under TUPE and whether they were members of a Defined Benefit pension scheme during their employment (with Voi UK or a prior employer). This impacts potential pension liabilities for Bolt. Employees currently in a Defined Contribution scheme would require employer contributions at least matching Voi UK's current level (4.5%) or employee contributions up to 6%.



# {color:#4c9aff}*IMPACT BEFORE THE TENDER CLARIFICATION PERIOD ENDS*{color}

*No Immediate Impact*: TUPE obligations will not take effect until Bolt begins providing services under the Agreement. There are no direct legal or operational obligations on Bolt before this point. The transferring employees would not join Bolt's workforce until the service commencement date, meaning no employment liabilities exist before then.

# {color:#4c9aff}*OBLIGATIONS IF BOLT IS THE SUCCESSFUL BIDDER*{color}

*Information and Consultation Process*: 

* Voi UK is responsible for initiating the TUPE-mandated information and consultation process with affected employees. Bolt, as the incoming contractor, must:

_Provide Voi UK with details of any "measures" it plans to implement concerning transferring employees. Examples include:_

_Proposed changes to terms and conditions._

_Adjustments to working arrangements._

_Any planned redundancies._

_Supply this information after receiving the existing employment terms of transferring employees from Voi UK._



{color:#4c9aff}*TO SUMMARISE* {color}

The Tender Agreement specifies that TUPE applies, and the Authority requires bidders to proceed on this basis. Therefore, you should factor this into your approach when bidding for the tender. Should Bolt be successful, TUPE obligations such as employee transfers and consultation processes will take effect when services commence, with advance preparation for compliance required during the transition period.

At this stage, prior to the tender clarification deadline, there are no TUPE-related liabilities or obligations impacting Bolt.

Please note, the advice obtained from external counsel was limited to the specific queries raised by Aisling. If further clarification on TUPE’s applicability, pensions, or Bolt’s potential liabilities is required, a more detailed assessment will be necessary as [~accountid:712020:a5b71bf1-1e62-42e6-8dd6-9e2a8e80227f] highlighted TUPE can be complex. However, you may determine that such an analysis is not essential before submitting your tender. You may want to have a further discussion with [~accountid:712020:a5b71bf1-1e62-42e6-8dd6-9e2a8e80227f]  to decide the best course of action for proceeding with this tender.
